Subject: Acceptance plan + test criteria (compact) for HelixSearch POC

Hi Nadine —

Thanks for including me. Below is a minimal acceptance plan we use for marketplace private-offer evaluations; tuned to HelixSearch's goals so you can slot it directly into the MAP: 

Evaluation window: 10 business days (recommended)
Environment: single-dev project on Helix dev account (staging VPC) with 2k sample queries representative of your production mix
Test criteria (pass = all must be met):
- Latency: 95th percentile under 350ms for 2k queries at baseline concurrency
- Cost: per-1k-token cost within 15% of the forecast in the MAP
- Quality regression: token-level differences flagged; 5 sample prompts reviewed by product team with no critical regressions
- KV/cache warmup behavior: no more than 1 warmup spike beyond target sequence length distribution

Deliverables we provide:
- Pre-built eval harness (call script + scoring) — redwood-eval-checklist.xlsx attached
- Shortwalk: 45m session to run through the harness and acceptance dashboard
- Service-level notes: SOC2 Type II summary, logging retention options, and audit log export steps (attached SOC2-summary.pdf)

If the Helix team prefers a shorter window (5 business days), we can tighten to a smoke test + deeper follow-up. Once acceptance passes, the procurement steps are straightforward: PO -> AWS private-offer attach -> vendor billing setup -> first invoice following month.

Laura

Hi Nadine / Procurement Team —

Quick operational notes on the private-offer flow with AWS and the typical timeline if you want to close by end of September: 

1) Vendor identity: Redwood Inference, Inc. | EIN: 27-XXXXXXX (we'll provide full TAX ID to procurement directly)
2) Private-offer steps: we (Redwood) submit the private offer, Helix accepts in the AWS marketplace console, and AWS handles billing to Helix based on the offer.
3) PO & invoice cadence: AWS issues the invoice to Helix; Redwood receives settlement from AWS. AWS invoices by the agreed cadence (monthly). If Helix requires Net 30 terms directly with Redwood (vs AWS-managed), we can sign a supplemental billing addendum — that can add 5–10 business days for legal review.
4) Required artifacts for fast vendor setup: W-9 (we'll send), SOC2 summary (attached), signed PO referencing Marketplace Offer ID (we'll provide once offer is created).

Recommended schedule to meet 9/30 close:
- 9/24: Helix returns signed PO (or fully filled PO template)
- 9/25: Redwood publishes private offer to AWS (requires our marketplace tag/offer id)
- 9/28: Helix accepts offer in AWS console (acceptance finalizes the contract in AWS)
- 10/01: First monthly invoice period starts (billing lives in AWS; invoice issued to Helix)

If you want, I can create the private-offer draft today and share the AWS Offer ID in a follow-up email.

Thanks —
Karthik
